label:
Inhalation lactose
(inhaler carrier)
comment: Lactose milled fine as the carrier powder the drug rides on.

about.text: Inhalation-grade lactose is crystalline alpha-lactose monohydrate, milled and sieved to a controlled particle size. Dry-powder inhalers use it as a carrier: a small amount of drug sticks to the coarse lactose grains, which make the dose easier to meter, and the drug is released into the airstream when the patient inhales.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

facts.v: Crystalline α-lactose monohydrate (spray-dried lactose carries up to 20 % amorphous lactose, so crystalline is preferred for stability)
Still the most widely used DPI carrier; drug particles stick to the big lactose crystals and are shaken off on inhalation
The production method strongly affects size, shape and solid form, so batches differ and carrier choice is largely empirical
Sold to Ph. Eur., USP-NF and JP specifications
